description: Illinois-only rules checked against the Illinois Vehicle Code and the Secretary of State GDL and zero-tolerance pages. National rules stay in the baseline. No fines.

questions.q: Unless another restriction is established, the maximum speed in an Illinois urban district is
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/11-601(c) sets 30 mph in an urban district, and 15 mph in an alley, unless some other speed restriction is established.

questions.q: Unless another restriction is established, the maximum speed in an Illinois alley is
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/11-601(c) sets 15 mph in an alley.

questions.q: Outside an urban district, 625 ILCS 5/11-601(d-1) sets the maximum on an interstate highway, including an Illinois toll highway, at
questions.explanation: Subsection (d-1) sets 70 mph on an interstate as defined in Section 1-133.1, including highways under the Illinois State Toll Highway Authority, unless another restriction is established. Cook, DuPage, Kane, Lake, Madison, McHenry, St. Clair, and Will counties may adopt a lower limit.

questions.q: Outside an urban district, the statutory maximum on Illinois highways that are not the 70 mph interstate or a designated divided highway in 11-601(d-1) is
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/11-601(d-1) sets 55 mph for all other highways, roads, and streets outside an urban district, unless another restriction is established.

questions.q: The special Illinois school-zone limit of 20 mph applies when
options: Every school zone is 20 mph all night
On school days, with children present and signs posted
It is 20 mph only while a bus is stopped
It replaces every posted limit within a mile of a school
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/11-605 sets 20 mph while passing a school zone, or on a public school roadway, when children are present and close enough to be a hazard. For this section a school day is 6:30 a.m. to 4 p.m. The limit does not apply unless the proper signs are posted.

questions.q: Under 625 ILCS 5/11-501, a person may not drive with an alcohol concentration of
questions.explanation: Section 11-501(a) prohibits driving or being in actual physical control of a vehicle when the alcohol concentration in blood, breath, or other bodily substance is 0.08 or more.

questions.q: Illinois zero tolerance applies to a driver under 21 who is cited for a traffic violation and has
options: A BAC of 0.08 or more only
A BAC of 0.02 or more only
questions.explanation: The Illinois Secretary of State says a driver under 21 with any trace of alcohol, a BAC of more than 0.00, loses driving privileges. A first offense is a 3-month suspension. A second offense is 1 year.

provenance.section: Zero Tolerance / Use It & Lose It

questions.q: A driver under 21 who refuses or fails to complete the zero-tolerance alcohol test faces, for a first violation,
options: No action until a court conviction
questions.explanation: The Secretary of State lists a first refusal or failure to complete the test as a 6-month suspension. A second refusal is 2 years.

questions.q: Driving an Illinois commercial motor vehicle with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.04 is
options: The same rule as a 0.08 non-commercial DUI and carries no CDL action
A first-violation CDL disqualification of not less than 12 months under 625 ILCS 5/6-514
Legal if the driver is over 21
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/6-514(a)(2) disqualifies a person from driving a commercial motor vehicle for not less than 12 months for a first violation of operating a CMV with an alcohol concentration of at least 0.04.

questions.q: Illinois does not suspend a license at a published demerit-point total for reckless driving. On the graduated-license page, the Secretary of State says two moving-violation convictions within 24 months result in
questions.explanation: The Secretary of State graduated-license page states that two moving-violation convictions within a 24-month period result in a minimum one-month suspension. The length depends on the seriousness of the offenses and the driver's history. Illinois does not publish a fixed point value for reckless driving.

questions.q: The nighttime restriction published by the Illinois Secretary of State for a graduated driver is
options: Midnight to 5 a.m. with no local variation
questions.explanation: The Secretary of State lists Sunday through Thursday, 10 p.m. to 6 a.m., and Friday to Saturday, 11 p.m. to 6 a.m. Local curfews may differ.

questions.q: Before an Illinois instruction-permit holder can get a graduated license, the Secretary of State requires practice of
questions.explanation: The permit must also be held for at least 9 months, and the practice is supervised by a parent or an adult age 21 or older who has a valid license.

questions.q: For the first 12 months of an Illinois graduated license, or until age 18, whichever comes first, passengers under 20 are limited to
questions.explanation: That is the passenger limit on the Secretary of State graduated-license page. A moving-violation conviction in that first year extends the one-unrelated-passenger limit for 6 months. One, unless the extra passengers are siblings, stepsiblings, children, or stepchildren of the driver.

questions.q: Illinois prohibits cell-phone use, including a hands-free device, for a driver under
questions.explanation: The Secretary of State says cell-phone use while driving, including a hands-free device, is prohibited for drivers under 19 except in an emergency.

questions.q: An Illinois graduated license is not issued to an applicant under 18 unless the applicant is at least 16 and has held a valid instruction permit for at least
questions.explanation: 625 ILCS 5/6-107 requires the applicant to be at least 16 and to have held a valid instruction permit for a minimum of 9 months.

questions.q: In Illinois, what is the youngest age at which you can get a learner's permit for a car?
questions.explanation: Illinois issues a learner's permit for a car at 15 years at the earliest.

questions.q: In Illinois, how long must a driver under 18 hold a learner's permit before moving to the next license?
questions.explanation: Illinois requires drivers under 18 to hold the learner's permit for 9 months.

questions.q: How many hours of supervised driving must a teen in Illinois complete before getting a provisional license?
questions.explanation: Illinois requires 50 hours of supervised driving before the provisional license.

questions.q: Of a Illinois teen's required supervised driving hours, how many must be at night?
questions.explanation: Illinois requires at least 10 hours of the supervised driving to be at night.

questions.q: In Illinois, what is the youngest age at which a teen can get a license to drive without a supervisor?
questions.explanation: In Illinois, the earliest unsupervised (provisional) license is at 16 years.

questions.q: In Illinois, what is the youngest age for a full, unrestricted car license?
questions.explanation: Illinois drivers can hold an unrestricted license at 18 years.

questions.q: How many questions are on the Illinois car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: The Illinois car knowledge test has 35 questions.

provenance.manual: Illinois Administrative Code 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80

questions.q: What score do you need to pass the Illinois car knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You need 80% to pass the Illinois car knowledge test.

provenance.manual: Illinois Administrative Code 92 Ill. Adm. Code 1030.80

questions.q: In Illinois, a driver 21 or older is legally impaired at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: In Illinois, drivers 21 and older are over the limit at 0.08% or more.

questions.q: In Illinois, a driver under 21 breaks the law at what blood alcohol concentration?
questions.explanation: Illinois sets the under-21 limit at 0.00%.

questions.q: In Illinois, how long is the license suspension for an adult's first refusal of a breath or blood test?
questions.explanation: A first refusal in Illinois brings a suspension of 1 year.

questions.q: What is the highest standard speed limit for cars on rural interstates in Illinois?
questions.explanation: Rural interstates in Illinois can be posted up to 70 mph for cars.

questions.q: Which best describes Illinois's law on drivers using a phone?
options: No statewide ban on phone use or texting
Hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers
Only texting is banned for all drivers
Phone use is banned only for new or young drivers
questions.explanation: Illinois: hand-held phone use is banned for all drivers.

questions.q: When is a left turn on a red light allowed in Illinois?
options: Only from a one-way street onto a one-way street
From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street
questions.explanation: In Illinois, a left turn on red (after a full stop, where not prohibited) is allowed: only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

questions.q: How is Illinois's seat belt law for adults enforced?
options: Secondary: police can cite you only after stopping you for something else
Primary: police can stop you just for not wearing a seat belt
No seat belt law for adults
questions.explanation: Illinois seat belt enforcement is primary.

questions.q: Until what age must a child ride in a car seat or booster seat in Illinois?
questions.explanation: Illinois requires a car seat or booster until 8 years, with height or weight exceptions.

provenance.manual: Safety Belts and Child Safety Seats

questions.q: What is Illinois's minimum liability insurance (injury per person / injury per crash / property damage)?
questions.explanation: Illinois requires at least $25,000 / $50,000 / $20,000.
